marking_verdicts.quantity: Servo supply configuration (rail count, settings, current)
marking_verdicts.reason: IOBoard.md:71 states exactly this: four TPS55285 a board, one per each of 3 servo rails (5.5 V/8.4 V settings, 4 to 6.35 A) plus one adjustable supply (0.8 to 15 V, 0.5 to 6.35 A), run from both the 12-20 V DC input and the pack, all owner-decided 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-30. Every figure lies inside the TPS55285's own registers per SLVSI72A, confirmed in round 1 (T1/009-P1-R6.json). Owner is correct.

marking_verdicts.quantity: Servo supply heatsink basis for continuous-current rating
marking_verdicts.reason: IOBoard.md:375 states 'A small aluminum heatsink on each TPS55285, on a 6-layer board (owner, 2026-09-30)' with no size, model or theta-JA given anywhere in the tree (confirmed by grep of Research.md and IOBoard.md). Owner decision, correctly marked.

marking_verdicts.quantity: Servo supply continuous current (TPS55285 + heatsink, 6.0 V in, 50 degC ambient)
marking_verdicts.reason: IOBoard.md:377 states this figure 'is not known: a follow-up of R6 finds it'. Supply.md:143 (the round-1 adjudicator's bound, FU-B1/030-adjudicator-R6.json) spans 89 to 179 degC against the 125 degC recommended max with no heatsink thermal-resistance figure, settling nothing. No source gives a value, so assumption (the catch-all for a quantity neither sourced with a figure nor an owner decision) is defensible, and the matching question is correctly raised.

125 degC recommended maximum (150 degC absolute) is confirmed in the round-1 adjudicator's reading of SLVSI72A section 5.2 (FU-B1/030-adjudicator-R6.json) and repeated in Supply.md:117, :134 and :143. IOBoard.md:460 itself references the same figure. The datasheet citation is one row removed from :460 (the number is not re-stated with 'SLVSI72A' literally on that line) but the figure is genuinely datasheet-sourced; sourced holds.

marking_verdicts.quantity: Servo rail voltage low end for brownout testing
marking_verdicts.reason: IOBoard.md:376: 'Each rail works down to the TPS55285's lowest output, 0.8 V, so a servo's brownout behavior can be tested (owner, 2026-09-30)'. Matches V55 (owner, 2026-09-30, Research.md:751) and lies inside the TPS55285's 0.8-21.3 V register range (SLVSI72A 5.2). Owner holds.

marking_verdicts.reason: 0.8 V comes from V55 (owner, 2026-09-30) and 8.4 V from the decided HV rail setting (IOBoard.md:376, owner). TPS259474LRPWR's VIN floor of 2.7 V (SLVSFC9C) fails the 0.8 V requirement, matching the round 2 Follow-ups row verbatim. Owner holds, and the matching question (index 0) is required and present.

FU-B1/002-P2-R6.json gives V122 = '3.0 A continuous: the per-servo current ceiling ... checked at every sample' sourced to docs/Servo.md:35 (Servo.md:35 confirms 'Current ceiling | 3.0 A | abort immediately, checked at every sample'), independent of rail voltage, so it still applies at 0.8-8.4 V. Note the line number is one off (Research.md:817 is V121's row; V122 is at :818), but the found value and its sourcing are correct, so sourced holds.

marking_verdicts.quantity: Port supply switch current/voltage-drop requirement at the 0.8 V brownout setting
marking_verdicts.reason: IOBoard.md:376 frames 0.8 V only as a brownout test point; no line states whether V122 (3.0 A) or V124 (570 mV, confirmed in FU-B1/002-P2-R6.json as built on the LV setting's 5.40 V edge and a 4.8 V lowest-rated LV servo, a premise that assumes a functioning, not failing, servo) extends to 0.8 V. marking_verdicts.quantity: Port voltage ceiling trip band and latch
marking_verdicts.reason: IOBoard.md:386 (state: 'decided (F16)') fixes the 6.0 V/8.7 V ceilings as an owner decision; V128 and V130 (FU-B1/002-P2-R6.json) narrow the band to 5.59/6.00 V and 8.53/8.70 V and confirm the latch-until-action rule, both confirmed verbatim. marking_verdicts.quantity: Servo supply temperature sensor part and placement
marking_verdicts.reason: IOBoard.md:460 states the MCP9808T-E/MS placement (4 a board, own I2C address in 0x18-0x1F apart from the onboard shunt's) as an owner decision dated 2026-09-30. The MCP9808 has 8 addresses in that range, so 4 fit. Owner holds; correctly deferring the shunt-address collision check to P5.

IOBoard.md:460 literally states 'The threshold is not stated: a follow-up of R6 sets it against the TPS55285's 125 degC recommended junction maximum', and no junction-to-sensor offset exists anywhere in the tree to derive a setpoint. No number is available, so assumption is a defensible classification, and the matching question (index 2, the follow-up gap verbatim) is correctly raised.

marking_verdicts.quantity: Already-selected R6 parts standing into round 2
marking_verdicts.reason: selection.json's R6 entries confirm I/O expander: MCP23017T-E/SS and Port supply switch: TPS259474LRPWR. The MCP23017's PCN refutation was overturned by the round-1 adjudicator (FU-B3/022-adjudicator-R6.json: Microchip's public PCN API shows no end-of-life notice among 43 matches), so it stands confirmed as stated. Sourced holds. (Research.md:313 is the R6 category-row text, which does not itself list these part numbers; the real support is selection.json and the cited FU-B3 files as the source field states, so the 'where' citation is loose, but the marking classification is correct.)

Supply.md:145 reads verbatim: 'R6, servo supply inductor, the selection record: selection.json keeps no part, although both FU-B3 verifiers confirm SRP1265A-4R7M (4.7 uH, 28 A saturation, 8.4 mOhm DC resistance at most, -55 to 150 degC) ... Not known why the confirmed part is not carried.' selection.json indeed has no part for this function. Sourced holds, and P1 is correct that round 2's Follow-ups table has no row for this function, so no new question is required here.
